title: Auto-run evaluations on model pin and config diffs with prioritization and lightweight smoke checks
creator: Sofia Morales
description:
Background: As customers pin catalog models or upgrade their pinned model versions, small behavioral regressions can silently degrade downstream application quality. Currently we run ad-hoc evals triggered manually by SRE/PM when a major catalog change is published. We need an automated system that triggers targeted eval workloads when either (a) a catalog model is updated/published or (b) a customer explicitly pins/upgrades a model version in their account, and that prioritizes quick smoke checks vs full regression suites to balance cost and detection velocity.

Goals: 
- Automatically trigger a tiered eval pipeline on model version pin/upgrades or config diffs that affect serving (quantization flags, sequence length defaults, tokenizers).
- Prioritize lightweight smoke tests (latency, basic prompt-set pass/fail, embedding similarity sanity) for immediate feedback, followed by full evaluation suites for higher-risk changes.
- Surface actionable regression alerts to customer-facing teams and expose a per-customer/regression dashboard in Console.
- Allow customers to opt-out of automated full eval runs for privacy/cost reasons but keep mandatory smoke checks for Verified models.

Scope & Non-Goals: 
- In scope: triggers on model-version changes in the catalog, customer pin actions in the Console/API, config diffs that affect runtime execution path (quantization, KV cache tuning, tokenizer changes). Integration points: Catalog service, Customer pin API, Eval orchestration, Console alerts dashboard.
- Out of scope: running private-customer full eval on proprietary prompt sets without explicit opt-in, or building new evaluation metrics beyond existing eval harness in the first phase.

Proposal details: 
1) Triggering events: publish/upgrade events from model-catalog and the customer pin endpoint should emit a standardized "eval.trigger" event with metadata: model_id, model_version, changed_configs, customer_id (if pinned), and risk_score (computed by catalog heuristics).
2) Tiered eval strategy: 
   - Tier 0 (mandatory smoke): <10 short prompts + latency & tokenization sanity checks + embedding drift quick-check. Target runtime: <10 minutes. Cost minimal. Runs for all catalog publishes and customer pins.
   - Tier 1 (targeted suite): a focused eval set per model family (e.g., summarization, instruction-following) chosen by catalog annotations. Target runtime: 30–90 minutes. Triggered for model_version changes with risk_score >= medium or when customer opts-in.
   - Tier 2 (full regression): the full regression harness used by Redwood for release gating. Runs only for catalog publish with high risk_score and for customer-requested audits.
3) Prioritization & throttling: Customer-pinned upgrades should be prioritized for that customer's tenant (fast smoke first). For catalog-wide publishes, run Tier 0 across models immediately and schedule Tier 1/2 on a queue with capacity-aware batching to avoid overloading eval infra.
4) Alerting & UX: 
   - Console: A new "Model Pin Eval" section in the Evals page showing recent evals triggered by pin/publish, pass/fail, delta metrics, and links to diffs and PRs. 
   - Notifications: PagerDuty opt-in for P0 regression from catalog publishes; Slack notifications to solutions/AMs for affected customers when a customer-pinned upgrade fails a Tier 0 smoke.
5) Opt-in/Opt-out and Data Controls: Customers can opt-out of Tier 1/2 full evals for cost/privacy; Tier 0 smoke checks required for pinned models only when the model is Redwood-verified or when the config diff touches runtime security / tokenizer changes.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Cost: running targeted evals for every pin could be expensive; mitigations: tiering, risk_score heuristics, capacity-aware scheduling, and customer opt-outs.
- Latency: Customers expect immediate feedback; we must ensure Tier 0 completes quickly and that Console surfaces pending statuses.
- Privacy/regulatory: Running evals with customer prompt sets requires explicit consent. Default to synthetic/shared prompt sets unless the customer provides test prompts.

Operational notes: 
- Owners: PM (Aisha), ENG (runtime & eval infra), Research (eval templates).
- Expected infra work: event wiring (catalog -> eval orchestrator), light weight eval container images, tagging of model families and associated eval suites, Console UI and notifications.
- Metrics: mean time-to-smoke (target < 10m), proportion of pin events that trigger Tier 1/2, false-positive alert rate, cost per triggered pin evaluation.

acceptance_criteria: When a customer pins or upgrades a model version via API/Console, an eval.trigger event is emitted with correct metadata
Tier 0 smoke runs automatically and completes within 10 minutes for >95% of pin events
Tier 1 queues are capacity-aware and do not exceed allocated eval infra budget thresholds
Console surfaces eval status for pins and links to the failing prompt examples when regressions detected
Customers can opt-out of Tier 1/2 while still receiving Tier 0 smoke results when required by verification policy
